source.note: Adults: start 20 mg/day in the morning; above 20 mg/day once daily or twice daily (morning and noon); 'should not exceed 80 mg/day' (so 80 mg twice daily would exceed the label).
'1 to 3 days after acute administration and 4 to 6 days after chronic administration'; norfluoxetine 4 to 16 days model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)

source.citation: Eugene AR. Fluoxetine pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution quantitatively supports a therapeutic role in COVID-19 at a minimum dose of 20 mg per day. F1000Research. 2022;10:477. doi:10.12688/f1000research.53275.3
source.note: 'The pharmacometric parameters referenced from the NDA were calculated by the FDA after combining 3 pharmacokinetic study datasets resulting in ... volume of distribution (Vd) value of 1,480 liters' (population PK estimate from the original Prozac NDA 18-936, Eli Lilly; not given per kg, so the weight slider is fixed).
single 40 mg dose: peak 'after 6 to 8 hours' model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)

source.citation: DrugBank DB00472 (Fluoxetine), Absorption/ADME summary, via PubChem CID 3386
source.note: 'The oral bioavailability of fluoxetine is <90% as a result of hepatic first pass metabolism.' (DrugBank, via PubChem). Stated only as an upper bound, not an exact figure -- US label gives no number at all. Used here as the model value, same upper-bound convention used for metoprolol's unchanged_fraction elsewhere in this dataset. Flagged for Anabella's review.
Lopressor (metoprolol) label: 'strong inhibitors of CYP2D6 such as quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine'. Prozac 7.7: 'Fluoxetine inhibits the activity of CYP2D6'. FDA table agrees (strong).

source.citation: FDA, 'For Healthcare Professionals | FDA's Examples of Drugs that Interact with CYP Enzymes and Transporter Systems' (content current as of 05/29/2026)
source.note: Table lists fluoxetine as '2C19; 2D6 strong inhibitor'.

'primary route of elimination appears to be hepatic metabolism to inactive metabolites excreted by the kidney' (no %). CYP2D6 is involved in its metabolism but its importance isn't stated, so no substrate entry. MISSING: bioavailability and Vd: labels and Canadian monographs only say 'large volume of distribution'; the Altamura 1994 review abstract gives no numbers.

journey.text: Absorbed from the gut; blood levels peak 6 to 8 hours after a dose.
Blocks serotonin from being taken back up by nerve cells in the brain, so more serotonin stays active.
Broken down in the liver into norfluoxetine, an active form that lasts even longer.
Leaves very slowly in urine as inactive pieces: active drug can remain for weeks after the last dose.
